feedback: Iteration 0 is a baseline with no race evidence, so this feedback is based on the contract rather than measured results. For the controller, I had to match the sensor weights to the sensor x order because the Builder's array is symmetric about the centre; the outer sensors carry the largest weights, so the signal stays bounded at about +/-2. I also had to pick a moderate kp so that a 12 mm pitch array does not over-steer when readings sit between 0 and 1. The 50 mm forward offset means the signal leads the wheels, so I added a small kd to damp the oscillation this lead could cause. The next race will show whether the array saturates (readings stuck at 0 or 1) and whether the outer sensors ever see the line. If line_loss_events are frequent or max_error nears 0.06 m, widen the sensor spread (for example x = +/-0.032) before changing the wheels. If the robot completes but completion_time is above 3 s, change the drivetrain (wheel_radius or mass) to gain speed. If steering_oscillation is high with no line loss, move sensors back toward the axle (y near 0.03) to reduce lead.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 on the s-bend or slalom, widen the sensor spread to x = +/-0.032 (keep pitch 16 mm) and keep sensor_size 0.012, since the outer pair at +/-0.024 may be missing the tape on offsets near 3 cm.

If completion_time exceeds 3 s on the oval with no line loss, reduce mass to 0.5 kg and/or wheel_radius to 0.035 to raise top speed; the baseline already uses the lowest in-range mass of 0.6 kg being at a usable minimum.
If steering_oscillation is high with a completed run, move the sensor row back to y = 0.03 to reduce the forward lead, as the 50 mm offset may cause lag on tight bends.
